clues: This town sits in the north east of New Zealand's South Island. It is the biggest town in its region.
This place is one of the sunniest in its whole country. Its summers are warm and dry, and its winters are cool and crisp.
Its name comes from a big battle that was fought in 1704. That fight was part of the War of the Spanish Succession.
In that 1704 fight, John Churchill led his troops to a great win. They beat French and Bavarian troops who fought side by side.
Wine made near this town is known all through its land. This area is the heart of the whole wine trade there.
